scope: Proposition 10.1 (Boundary arch mass) of the manuscript “Signed cylinder propagation and marked polygons on the honeycomb lattice” (preprints/Signed-cylinder-propagation-and-marked-polygons-on-the-honeycomb-lattice-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2dda2109318f92bb), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 76. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a port on a horizontal tessellation half-plane boundary. Let WR be the total critical weight xN of first-exit same-boundary arches reaching Euclidean distance at least R from that port. Then WR = R−1/4+o(1). If H(d) is the mass of arches ending d boundary steps to the right, then 2 sin(π/8) X d>0 H(d) = 1, X d≥n H(d) ≤ n−1/4+o(1) . The constants are unchanged by lattice translations and rotations.
